one_line: Better Stack walkthrough of xAI's recent releases: Grok 4.6 benchmarks and cost, Grok Imagine image and video editing, Grok Build and Cursor, and a voice agent builder. Main takeaway: list price is not total cost.
summary: The presenter argues xAI has been shipping quickly since the SpaceX merger and the Cursor acquisition, and is worth evaluating again for software work. Grok 4.6 ranks fourth on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and second on GDPval and Terminal-Bench, at $2 in and $6 out. The presenter's cost chart shows 4.6 burns more tokens per completed task than 4.5 at the same list price, so real spend rises. Grok Imagine's image editing is the strongest part of the demo: segment-level editing, virtual try-on from multiple images, and image-to-video with a consistent character. The harness story is fragmented (Grok Build CLI, GrokBots, and Grok inside Cursor), and the presenter says Grok 4.6 in Cursor is good at software engineering. The voice agent builder can use web search, Gmail and custom MCP tools, but phone-number and custom-voice features were not testable in his region. The evidence is one presenter's demos and vendor-supplied benchmark charts, with no reproducible commands.

key_ideas.idea: xAI has been shipping quickly in recent months after the SpaceX merger and the Cursor purchase, and the presenter now considers it a serious coding contender.
key_ideas.detail: The intro lists Grok 4.7, Grok Imagine, Grok Build and a voice agent builder. The review then covers only Grok 4.6, so the 4.7 claim is not examined.

key_ideas.idea: Grok 4.6 moved up sharply on composite and task benchmarks at $2 in and $6 out.
key_ideas.detail: Fourth on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, near GPT-5.6 and Opus. Second on GDPval (real-world tasks; previously about 12th), behind Opus 5. Second on Terminal-Bench. The presenter reads the jump from 4.5 to 4.6 as large but does not say the exact score values.

key_ideas.idea: Same list price does not mean same cost: 4.6 burns more tokens per completed task than 4.5.
key_ideas.detail: The intelligence-versus-cost chart uses a log cost axis and scores end-to-end completion of complex tasks. 4.5 sat in the most attractive quadrant. 4.6 is more intelligent and more expensive at identical per-token pricing, which the presenter attributes to more internal reasoning tokens.

key_ideas.idea: Grok Imagine's video pricing and speed are the headline claims, but the presenter did not test them.
key_ideas.detail: Per the vendor's own chart, video costs about 7 cents per second and generates in about 45 seconds. The presenter also cites a second comparison figure for Sora 2 Pro, but the transcript garbles it. The presenter says Sora was recently shut down for cost, which he states as "I believe".

key_ideas.idea: Grok Imagine's per-element editing is the most useful UI idea in the video.
key_ideas.detail: After generation, the image is split into segments (leaves, icons, brush strokes, bowls) listed in a side panel. Clicking one element and writing a new prompt changes only that element, which avoids regenerating the whole image.

key_ideas.idea: Multi-image virtual try-on and product-to-video work with the presenter's own photos.
key_ideas.detail: A garment photo and a person photo are combined with a template, and the result keeps the outfit on the person. A marathon photo worked too. The same product-plus-person input can produce video in which only one element changes while the character stays consistent. Sketch-to-3D and prototype generation are also offered through the API.

key_ideas.idea: Grok's harness products are fragmented, and Grok 4.6 inside Cursor is the presenter's working setup.
key_ideas.detail: Grok Build is a terminal CLI in the same category as Claude Code and Codex CLI. GrokBots is closer to Claude Cowork and can drive a machine and browse. Cursor now promotes Grok 4.6, offers Composer 2.5 and Claude models, and has a router that picks a model in auto mode. The presenter says the products will likely converge. He used Grok 4.6 in Cursor for a week and calls it good at software engineering, and cheaper than Opus through API rates.

key_ideas.idea: The voice agent builder combines a voice, tools and a phone number into a deployable agent.
key_ideas.detail: Builders attach tools such as web search, Gmail and custom MCP servers, pick a voice, and can attach a phone number. The live demo gave a fast restaurant recommendation and handled interruptions. Phone numbers and custom voice training were unavailable in the presenter's region, so they were not tested.

techniques.name: Compare models by cost per completed task, not list price
techniques.how: Run a complex end-to-end task on each candidate model and measure total tokens and spend. The presenter's chart uses that method, and it shows the same-price model can cost more. Use the Artificial Analysis cost-versus-intelligence view as a starting point.
techniques.when: Choosing or re-routing a model when a version bump keeps the per-token price the same, or when a router sends requests to a model by default.

techniques.name: Element-level re-prompting of a generated image
techniques.how: Generate the image, open the segment list in the side panel, click one element, and describe only that change (for example, a flower instead of a leaf). The rest of the image is unchanged.
techniques.when: Iterating on a generated graphic when only one part is wrong, such as a flyer or product mockup.

techniques.name: Multi-image virtual try-on with a template
techniques.how: Provide a person photo and a product or garment photo, use the built-in template, and generate. For video, provide the same inputs and edit one element while keeping the character consistent. The exact prompt and parameters were not shown.
techniques.when: Product mockups, fashion try-on, or short product videos that need a consistent person across shots.

techniques.name: Voice agent with tools and a phone number
techniques.how: Create an agent in the voice builder, attach tools (web search, Gmail, or a custom MCP server), select a voice, and optionally attach a phone number. Test live with the in-browser voice chat before attaching a number.
techniques.when: Customer support or reservation agents that need live data and must be reachable by phone. Check regional availability of phone numbers and custom voices first.

numbers.claim: Grok 4.6 pricing is $2 input and $6 output (units not stated; presumably per million tokens).
Grok 4.6 is fourth on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. It was about 12th on GDPval before and is now second, behind Opus 5. It is second on Terminal-Bench.
4.5 and 4.6 have the same list price, but 4.6 burns more tokens per completed task, so cost rises with intelligence.
Grok Imagine video is about 7 cents per second and generates in about 45 seconds, per xAI's own comparison chart against Sora 2 Pro. The Sora figure is garbled in the transcript.

hot_takes: xAI is "killing it" and is a serious coding contender again (title and intro, based on release cadence and one week of use).
Grok Imagine's image output beats ChatGPT and Gemini on the flyer test (one prompt, one presenter).
Grok Build, GrokBots and Cursor will likely converge into one product (speculation).
Sora was shut down because it was too expensive to run (presenter says "I believe").

relevance.why: AgentOS budgets and strategy routing need cost per task, and this video shows a same-price model version raising token burn per task.
relevance.action: When adding a model version to strategy routing, track cost per completed task (tokens and spend on a fixed end-to-end task), not only the per-token list price.

relevance.why: Grok Build is another terminal coding harness similar to Claude Code, but the video shows no harness internals relevant to checkpointing, planning or approvals.
